title: What the Reality-to-Data Mapping Engine is
description: The engine builds a structured representation where real-world observations, instrument measurements, scientific models, and digital records are linked together explicitly. A temperature reading is not just a number — it is a number tied to a sensor, a calibration record, a location, a time, and the model that interprets it. That linkage is what makes the representation checkable.

architecture: An observation graph stores entities (sensors, places, times) and edges (measured, calibrated-by, interpreted-by); a mapping layer binds raw values to typed quantities with units; validation rules reject physically impossible mappings.

title: Observation and measurement data model
description: Every observation is a first-class record: who or what observed, with which instrument, under what calibration, at what place and time, with what uncertainty. title: Sensor fusion algorithm
description: Multiple sensors observing the same quantity are fused into one estimate weighted by each sensor's calibrated uncertainty. A cheap sensor with wide error bars contributes less than a calibrated instrument. The fused estimate carries a combined uncertainty that honestly reflects disagreement between sensors.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Sensor fusion algorithm

architecture: Inverse-variance weighting over synchronized readings; outlier rejection when a sensor disagrees beyond its stated uncertainty; fused output with propagated uncertainty.

title: Model-to-observation alignment algorithm
description: Scientific models make predictions; observations test them. The alignment algorithm pairs each model prediction with the observations that bear on it, computes residuals, and flags systematic mismatch. A model that consistently misses in one direction is not just noisy — it is wrong in a way the engine can characterize.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Model-to-observation alignment algorithm

architecture: Prediction registry keyed by (model, conditions); observation matcher by time/place/conditions; residual analyzer distinguishing noise from systematic bias.

title: Plausibility reasoning: rejecting impossible mappings
description: A mapping that claims water boiled at 20 degrees Celsius at sea level is wrong, and the engine should say so without being asked. Plausibility rules encode physical constraints — valid ranges, conservation checks, unit consistency — and every ingested mapping passes through them before it enters the representation.

description: A river station reports temperature, dissolved oxygen, and flow every 15 minutes. Every number in the summary traces back to a reading.

title: Failure modes: calibration lapse and silent drift
description: Sensors drift, calibrations lapse, and adapters fail silently. The engine treats these as expected events: calibration-aware validity windows automatically quarantine readings outside them, drift detectors compare redundant sensors, and adapter heartbeats raise alarms on silence. The map degrades gracefully instead of confidently wrong.

title: Security: protecting the chain of custody
description: A provenance chain is only trustworthy if it cannot be tampered with. Observations are hash-chained at ingest, calibration certificates are signed, and every reinterpretation is recorded as a new layer rather than an edit. Auditors can verify the whole chain without trusting the engine's word.
